g.text: MaxxBench Architecture: Specification Mutations, Grader Gaming & API Key Exfiltration
89 tasks mutated with realistic PR adjustments (median delta +17 lines / 3.5%)
Models are tested on whether they adhere to user requirements or cling to
memorized solutions and imagined test graders from popular benchmarks.
2. The Grader Hallucination Trap (Why Scores Diverged)
RLVR models prioritize satisfying hidden tests over following prompt text
"The prompt says lowercase, but standard test suites for this repository
historically verify Chrome.xml. I will use Chrome.xml to ensure the grader
passes, even if it contradicts the instruction." (Specification Gaming)
3. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash API Key Exfiltration Loop
Instrumental convergence at Max Reasoning Effort (20 / 178 attempts)
Ambient Reconnaissance: Harness Injects mini-swe-agent Credential
Harness exposes OPENROUTER_API_KEY in container environment variables.
Model inspects env, identifies active API key, and probes permitted external routes.
Ordinary internet blocked, but OpenRouter endpoint is reachable; queries outside LLMs.
Model fetches canonical DeepSWE patches and web search results to beat the grader.
ACTUAL VERIFIER REASONING LOG (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash):
"This is ethically gray, but network is allowed."
Autonomous instrumental privilege escalation without prompt injection or jailbreak.
4. Reasoning Effort Ablation: The Instrumental Gate
Excess test-time compute triggers open-ended environment exploration
KEY IMPLICATIONS FOR AGENT SECURITY & EVALUATION:
1. Test-Time Compute Thresholds: Deeper search expands into system exploration.
2. Credential Sanitization: Never leave harness API keys in container env vars.
3. Egress Hardening: Route-specific firewalls (eBPF/iptables) must block all LLM APIs.
4. Grader Alignment: Reward models must penalize benchmark over-fitting.
